record.body: Superb lyrebirds of Australia are famous mimics: a male's song can include convincing imitations of other bird species, and also of non-bird sounds heard in its environment, woven into long display songs during courtship. Mimicry can function in mate attraction, with females preferring males with larger or more accurate repertoires, and in some species mimicry also serves deception, as when a bird imitates a predator's alarm call to scatter competitors. Not every sound a lyrebird makes is mimicry, and careful studies separate genuine imitation from species-typical song elements that merely sound similar. This record covers the biophony layer: every mimicked sound, whatever its original source, is a living bird's vocalisation when the lyrebird produces it, while the original environmental sounds belong to their own layers.

demo.code:
TITLE = "Vocal Mimicry and Deception: The Lyrebird's Repertoire"
BANDS = {'own song': 8, 'mimicked birds': 12, 'other sounds': 4}
tot = float(sum(BANDS.values()))
print('Record: ' + TITLE)
print('Total: %d' % int(tot))
for k in sorted(BANDS):
    print('%s: %d (%.1f percent)' % (k, BANDS[k], 100.0 * BANDS[k] / tot))

other sounds: 4 (16.7 percent)
own song: 8 (33.3 percent)
